detailed_summary: This paper introduces a weighted-shift formulation of bivariate bicycle group-algebra (BBGA) codes over finite group algebras, generalizing the standard bivariate bicycle (BB) construction. The key idea is to use two binary shifts: one acting by right multiplication and the other by left multiplication. Associativity ensures these shifts commute even when the seed group is nonabelian, allowing bivariate polynomials in the shifts (including mixed monomials) to define CSS codes. The authors derive explicit sparsity bounds and distinguish nonabelian seed groups from codes that are intrinsically inequivalent to abelian realizations. For the dihedral group D3, a pair of weighted permutation shifts generates a regular C6×C12 action and recovers the known [[144,12,12]] and [[144,14,14]] bivariate bicycle codes. They also present a computer-verified [[144,16,12]] code over A4×C6 with every check of weight eight, which belongs to the established nonabelian two-block group-algebra family. Exhaustive low-weight enumeration and an intrinsic stabilizer-support invariant certify that this code is inequivalent to any ordinary abelian BB or two-block group-algebra realization, even under qubit permutations combined with local Clifford operations. Finally, a nonuniform weighted-shift construction over F2[C3] yields a [[18,4,3]] code with check weights six and eight. An exact enumeration of its minimum stabilizer supports rules out every ordinary binary 2BGA realization at that length under the same equivalence, establishing that the unrestricted weighted-shift formulation extends beyond the ordinary 2BGA class even with an abelian seed group.
key_contributions: Introduces a weighted-shift formulation of bivariate bicycle group-algebra codes that allows nonabelian seed groups by using left and right multiplication shifts, with associativity guaranteeing commutation.
Provides explicit sparsity bounds for the resulting CSS codes and distinguishes nonabelian seed groups from codes intrinsically inequivalent to abelian realizations.
Recovers known [[144,12,12]] and [[144,14,14]] bivariate bicycle codes via a regular C6×C12 action from D3 weighted permutation shifts.

Constructs a computer-verified [[144,16,12]] code over A4×C6 with all checks of weight eight, and proves its inequivalence to any ordinary abelian BB or two-block group-algebra realization using exhaustive low-weight enumeration and an intrinsic stabilizer-support invariant.

Presents a nonuniform weighted-shift construction over F2[C3] yielding a [[18,4,3]] code with check weights six and eight, and rules out every ordinary binary 2BGA realization at that length via exact enumeration of minimum stabilizer supports.
methodology_analysis: The paper employs algebraic and computational methods. The core construction uses group algebras over F2, with two shifts defined by right and left multiplication by group elements. Associativity ensures these shifts commute, enabling the definition of bivariate polynomials that yield CSS codes. The authors analyze sparsity by bounding the weights of the check operators. To certify inequivalence, they use exhaustive low-weight enumeration of stabilizer supports and an intrinsic stabilizer-support invariant, which is invariant under qubit permutations and local Clifford operations. They also perform computer-verified searches for specific codes, such as the [[144,16,12]] code over A4×C6, and exact enumeration for the [[18,4,3]] code over F2[C3]. The methodology combines theoretical derivation with computational verification to establish both the existence of new codes and their inequivalence to known families.
results_analysis: The paper reports several concrete results. It recovers the known [[144,12,12]] and [[144,14,14]] bivariate bicycle codes from a D3-based weighted-shift construction, demonstrating that the new formulation encompasses existing codes. The new [[144,16,12]] code over A4×C6 has a higher logical qubit count (16) compared to the recovered codes, with all checks of weight eight, and is proven inequivalent to any abelian BB or two-block group-algebra realization. The [[18,4,3]] code over F2[C3] has check weights six and eight and is shown to be outside the ordinary binary 2BGA class. These results indicate that the weighted-shift formulation can produce codes with parameters not achievable by standard abelian constructions, even when the seed group is abelian. The inequivalence proofs rely on exhaustive enumeration and invariants, providing strong evidence for the novelty of these codes.
strengths: The formulation elegantly generalizes bivariate bicycle codes to nonabelian groups using left and right multiplication shifts, with a clear algebraic foundation.
The paper provides rigorous inequivalence proofs using exhaustive enumeration and an intrinsic invariant, which is a strong certification of novelty.
It includes concrete, computer-verified examples with specific parameters, demonstrating the practical utility of the construction.
The recovery of known codes and the discovery of new ones show that the framework is both encompassing and extending existing families.
limitations: The paper focuses on small examples and specific groups; scalability to larger codes and general nonabelian groups is not fully explored.
The computational verification, while rigorous for the given examples, may not be feasible for larger codes due to exponential complexity.
The practical performance of these codes (e.g., error thresholds under decoding) is not analyzed, leaving their utility for fault-tolerant quantum computing uncertain.
connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics, particularly quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing. The construction of CSS codes from group algebras connects to algebraic coding theory and quantum stabilizer codes. The use of nonabelian groups and weighted shifts introduces new algebraic structures that could lead to codes with better parameters or new properties. The inequivalence results highlight the importance of algebraic invariants in classifying quantum codes, which is a topic of interest in quantum information theory. Overall, the paper contributes to the ongoing effort to design efficient quantum LDPC codes with good parameters.
overall_assessment: The paper presents a novel and technically sound generalization of bivariate bicycle codes to nonabelian group algebras via weighted shifts. The construction is elegant, and the results are rigorously verified, including inequivalence proofs that establish the novelty of the new codes. The recovery of known codes and the discovery of a [[144,16,12]] code with all checks of weight eight are significant. However, the work is limited to small examples and lacks analysis of decoding performance or scalability. Despite these limitations, the paper makes a valuable contribution to quantum error correction by expanding the design space of quantum LDPC codes and providing a framework for constructing codes beyond the abelian regime.
